paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches: a heart doesn't drift off all at once. Solomon had the wisdom, the riches and a God who had appeared to him twice (1 Kings 11:9). Yet the text says his wives "turned his heart after other gods," and he "was not wholeheartedly devoted to the LORD his God, as his father David had been" (1 Kings 11:4). The warning was clear, and he still clung to what the LORD had said not to cling to (1 Kings 11:2).

So here's the question for you, baker. Gifts are not the same as devotion. Solomon could have all the wisdom in the world and still let his heart wander, and I think that's the scary part. A cookie can look perfect and still be undercooked in the middle, and a heart can look fine from the outside too. The LORD looked at where Solomon's heart was, not at how impressive the kingdom looked (1 Kings 11:9).

But look at what else the LORD does. Even while He speaks of tearing the kingdom away, He says, "for the sake of your father David," and He leaves one tribe for Solomon's son, for the sake of "Jerusalem, which I have chosen" (1 Kings 11:12-13). That tells me the LORD keeps His word to His people even when the people don't keep theirs. So guard your heart, friend, stay wholeheartedly with Him, and remember that the LORD who holds you is faithful.
